title: Defence Acquisition Council Approves ₹52,000 Crore Military Procurement Including Kamikaze Drones and MP-ATGM
summary: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by the Defence Minister, approved military purchases worth ₹52,000 crore. The procurement package includes kamikaze (loitering munition) drones and anti-tank weapons. Notably, DRDO's indigenously developed Multi-Platform Anti-Tank Guided Missile (MP-ATGM), after a decade of development, is poised for induction into the armed forces following this approval.
exam_angle: DAC is the apex body for defence capital acquisitions in India; this approval reflects India's push for atmanirbharta in defence under the Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) and DRDO's role in indigenous weapons development.
key_facts: Total approval: ₹52,000 crore
Items include: kamikaze drones, anti-tank weapons
MP-ATGM: DRDO-developed, 10-year development cycle
DAC: Apex defence procurement body under Ministry of Defence

title: India Reaffirms Indus Waters Treaty 'In Abeyance' Amid Pakistan Tensions; MEA Stays Firm
summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs reiterated that the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) of 1960 remains 'in abeyance,' maintaining its position unchanged despite Pakistan's warnings and threats. India stated that Pakistan must stop backing terrorism as a precondition for normalisation, and also conveyed its views on the Teesta river issue. Pakistan rejected India's assertions, calling them 'baseless allegations of terrorism.'
exam_angle: The Indus Waters Treaty (brokered by World Bank, 1960) and its current suspension are critical for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (water security); connects to India-Pakistan bilateral relations and cross-border terrorism.
key_facts: Indus Waters Treaty signed: 1960, brokered by World Bank
India declared IWT 'in abeyance' post-Pahalgam attack (April 2026)
MEA: India's stand remains unchanged
Pakistan rejected India's terrorism linkage as 'baseless'

title: India-Japan Sign Strategic Defence and Technology Pacts; China Cautions Against Third-Party Targeting
summary: India and Japan unveiled an ambitious strategic roadmap covering defence cooperation and critical minerals, with both countries signing significant pacts on defence technology and industry. The UNICORN pact, a separate agreement, involves Japanese stealth technology to reduce the radar signature of Indian Navy warships. China cautioned that India-Japan ties should not target any third party and objected to the 'Free and Open Indo-Pacific' framing. The 75th anniversary of India-Japan diplomatic ties will be celebrated in 2027 with cultural events.
exam_angle: India-Japan defence and tech partnerships are key for GS Paper 2 (IR); connects to Indo-Pacific strategy, Quad, and India's critical minerals policy; UNICORN pact links to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Defence).
key_facts: UNICORN pact: Japanese stealth technology for Indian Navy warships
Cooperation areas: defence, critical minerals, technology
China objected: ties should not target third parties
75th anniversary of India-Japan diplomatic relations: 2027

title: India's Forex Reserves Fall $5.65 Billion Amid West Asia War Impact
summary: India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $5.65 billion, attributed in part to the geopolitical impact of the ongoing West Asia conflict involving Iran. The fall reflects pressure on the rupee and increased import costs, particularly for crude oil. Despite the dip, India's crude oil inventory simultaneously hit an almost one-year high due to strong import volumes, indicating active stock-building ahead of anticipated supply disruptions.
exam_angle: Forex reserves and their management by RBI are key for GS Paper 3 (Economy); connects to current account deficit, crude oil import dependence, and the geopolitical-economic nexus.
key_facts: Forex reserves fell by: $5.65 billion
Reason: Iran war geopolitical impact, rupee pressure
India's crude inventory: hit almost 1-year high
RBI manages forex reserves as lender of last resort

title: India Targets $1 Trillion in Exports for FY26; Piyush Goyal Urges States to Identify Import Substitution Goods
summary: India has set an ambitious $1 trillion export target for FY2025-26, combining merchandise and services trade. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that Indian firms must leave their 'comfort zone' to achieve this target and urged states to identify goods currently being imported that could be manufactured domestically. This aligns with India's broader push for import substitution and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
exam_angle: Export targets and trade policy connect to GS Paper 3 (Economy); relevant to India's foreign trade policy, Make in India, and Atmanirbhar Bharat framework.
key_facts: Export target for FY26: $1 trillion (merchandise + services combined)
Commerce Minister: Piyush Goyal
States urged to identify imported goods for domestic manufacturing
Connects to Atmanirbhar Bharat and PLI schemes

title: India-France Economic and Financial Dialogue Co-Chaired by Nirmala Sitharaman in Aix-en-Provence
summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman co-chaired the India-France Economic and Financial Dialogue (EFD) with French Economy Minister Roland Lescure in Aix-en-Provence, France. The EFD is a structured bilateral mechanism for discussing macroeconomic, financial, and trade issues. This dialogue comes amid broader India-France strategic partnership deepening across defence, energy, and digital sectors.
exam_angle: Bilateral economic dialogues are important for GS Paper 2 (IR); India-France is a strategic partnership with significance in defence, nuclear energy, and multilateral forums like G20.
key_facts: Forum: India-France Economic and Financial Dialogue (EFD)
Venue: Aix-en-Provence, France
India represented by: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman
France represented by: Minister Roland Lescure

title: Government Debunks E20 Ethanol Blending 'Myths'; Public Backlash Triggers Political Controversy
summary: The Indian government issued clarifications debunking viral claims that E20 fuel (20% ethanol blended petrol) damages engines or wastes water, calling them misinformation. The controversy was triggered after a minister used the word 'experiment' in reference to the ethanol blending programme, sparking public backlash. Opposition leader Arvind Kejriwal urged the PM to roll back the E20 programme. The government reiterated that E20 is a proven fuel standard, part of the National Biofuels Policy.
exam_angle: Ethanol blending policy (E20 target by 2025, now E20 rollout) is a key component of India's energy security and National Biofuels Policy 2018; relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy/Environment).
key_facts: E20: 20% ethanol blended with 80% petrol
Programme under: National Biofuels Policy 2018
Nodal ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
India's ethanol blending target: E20 by 2025 (now in implementation)

title: New Gold Monetisation Scheme in the Works to Reduce Gold Import Dependence
summary: The Indian government is working on a revamped Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS) aimed at mobilising idle household gold and reducing dependence on gold imports. India is one of the world's largest gold importers, and the scheme seeks to bring domestically held gold into the formal financial system. The original GMS was launched in 2015; the new version is expected to offer improved interest rates and easier redemption mechanisms.
exam_angle: Gold Monetisation Scheme connects to India's current account deficit management, reducing import bill, and financial inclusion; relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy) and government schemes.
key_facts: Original Gold Monetisation Scheme launched: 2015
Objective: Mobilise idle gold, reduce gold imports
India is among world's top gold importers (~800-900 tonnes/year)
New scheme expected to have improved interest rates and redemption options

title: India's Oldest Accurately Dated Banyan Tree (700 Years Old) Discovered in Bihar's Munger
summary: Scientists, with support from the Department of Science and Technology (DST), have identified a 700-year-old Banyan tree in Munger, Bihar, as the oldest accurately dated Banyan tree in India and possibly the world. The dating was done using scientific methods, making it a landmark discovery in botanical and heritage conservation. The Banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is India's national tree.
exam_angle: Connects to biodiversity conservation, India's national symbols, and scientific dating methods; DST's role in scientific research is relevant; Ficus benghalensis as national tree is a static GS fact.
key_facts: Location: Munger, Bihar
Age: ~700 years (oldest accurately dated Banyan in India)
Scientific body involved: Department of Science and Technology (DST)
Banyan (Ficus benghalensis): India's national tree

title: Government Orders Removal of Three Apps Used to Remotely Disable E-Rickshaws
summary: The Indian government has ordered the removal of three mobile applications — BAT-BMS, Lossigy, and Epoch-i-ion — which were being misused by battery manufacturers or financiers to remotely disable e-rickshaws, allegedly to enforce loan repayments. This action is aimed at protecting e-rickshaw operators, many of whom are from economically weaker sections, from predatory digital practices. The move falls under consumer protection and digital regulation frameworks.
exam_angle: Connects to consumer protection law, digital governance, and EV ecosystem regulation in India; also relevant to informal sector workers' rights and GS Paper 2 (Governance).
key_facts: Apps ordered removed: BAT-BMS, Lossigy, Epoch-i-ion
Misuse: Remotely disabling e-rickshaws (loan recovery tool)
Action taken by: Central Government (Ministry of Electronics/Consumer Affairs)
Affected: E-rickshaw operators, mostly from weaker economic sections

title: Monsoon Session of Parliament 2026 to Begin July 20 with High-Stakes Legislative Agenda
summary: The Monsoon Session of Parliament of India is scheduled to begin on July 20, 2026. The session is expected to have a high-stakes legislative agenda, potentially including key bills. Parliament's Monsoon Session is typically held from July to August each year and is one of three sessions (Budget, Monsoon, Winter) of Parliament.
exam_angle: Parliamentary sessions, their scheduling, and legislative procedures are core to GS Paper 2 (Polity); the Monsoon Session date and agenda are relevant for current affairs.
key_facts: Monsoon Session 2026 start date: July 20
Parliament has three sessions: Budget (Feb-May), Monsoon (Jul-Aug), Winter (Nov-Dec)
Session scheduling: decided by Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs
Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha both convene during sessions

title: Supreme Court Declines to Stay Bail of Sonam Raghuvanshi in Meghalaya Honeymoon Murder Case
summary: The Supreme Court of India refused to stay or cancel the bail granted to Sonam Raghuvanshi, accused in the Meghalaya 'honeymoon murder case.' The SC upheld the bail order amid confusion about procedural aspects of the bail hearing. The case involves the alleged murder of a husband during a honeymoon trip in Meghalaya, with the wife as the prime accused.
exam_angle: Supreme Court's bail jurisprudence and the right to liberty (Article 21) are key constitutional issues; SC's power to cancel bail and principles of bail under CrPC/BNSS are exam-relevant.
key_facts: Court: Supreme Court of India
Decision: Refused to stay/cancel bail of Sonam Raghuvanshi
Case: Meghalaya honeymoon murder case
Bail provisions: Under BNSS (formerly CrPC); Article 21 — right to life and liberty

title: IT Minister Orders MeitY to Summon Meta Over Child Abuse Advertisements on Instagram
summary: Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw directed the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to summon Meta (parent company of Instagram) over reports of child sexual abuse-related advertisements appearing on Instagram. This action invokes India's IT Act provisions on harmful content and intermediary liability. It reflects growing government scrutiny of social media platforms under the IT Rules 2021.
exam_angle: IT Act 2000, IT Rules 2021, intermediary liability, and child safety online are key for GS Paper 2 (Governance/Social Justice); MeitY's regulatory role over social media is exam-relevant.
key_facts: Minister involved: Ashwini Vaishnaw (IT Minister)
Action: MeitY directed to summon Meta (Instagram's parent)
Issue: Child sexual abuse material/advertisements on Instagram
Regulatory framework: IT Act 2000, IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021

title: CSIR-SERC Partners with Merlin Automation Solutions to Advance 3D Concrete Printing Technology in India
summary: CSIR's Structural Engineering Research Centre (CSIR-SERC) has signed a partnership with Merlin Automation Solutions to advance 3D concrete printing technology in India. This collaboration aims to develop affordable and scalable construction techniques using additive manufacturing, which can accelerate housing construction and reduce costs. 3D concrete printing is seen as a disruptive technology for India's affordable housing mission.
exam_angle: CSIR's technology transfer and public-private partnerships in sci-tech are relevant for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech); 3D printing in construction connects to affordable housing and innovation ecosystem.
key_facts: Partners: CSIR-SERC and Merlin Automation Solutions
Technology: 3D Concrete Printing (additive manufacturing in construction)
CSIR-SERC: Structural Engineering Research Centre, Chennai
Application: Affordable housing, faster construction

title: Europe Heatwave Kills Over 2,000 in France; Climate Change Made Event 2.5°C Hotter
summary: France recorded 2,025 excess deaths at the peak of a record-breaking heatwave, with Europe bracing for more extreme weather events. Scientists attributed the severity of the heatwave to climate change, which made the June event up to 2.5°C hotter than it would have been without anthropogenic warming. The findings come from rapid climate attribution studies and highlight the accelerating frequency of extreme heat events in Europe.
exam_angle: Climate attribution science and extreme weather events are important for GS Paper 3 (Environment) and GS Paper 1 (Geography); connects to IPCC findings, Paris Agreement targets, and climate justice discourse.
key_facts: France excess deaths: 2,025 at heatwave peak
Climate change contribution: Made event up to 2.5°C hotter
Scientific method: Rapid climate attribution analysis
Trend: Extreme heat events increasing in frequency and intensity due to global warming

title: India's Exotic Pet Trade Growing; Regulation Gaps Exposed Under Wildlife Protection Act
summary: A report highlights India's rapidly growing exotic pet trade, which is exploiting significant regulatory gaps in the Wildlife Protection Act (WPA) 1972. Many exotic species sold in India are not native and thus may not be covered under Schedule I-IV of the WPA, creating loopholes. The trade poses risks of invasive species introduction, zoonotic disease spread, and threatens biodiversity conservation efforts.
exam_angle: Wildlife Protection Act 1972, CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species), and invasive species are key environment topics for GS Paper 3; regulatory gaps in wildlife trade connect to GS Paper 2 (Governance).
key_facts: Regulatory framework: Wildlife Protection Act (WPA) 1972
Loophole: Non-native/exotic species not covered under WPA schedules
International framework: CITES regulates cross-border wildlife trade
Risks: Invasive species, zoonotic diseases, biodiversity loss

title: India Contests US 'Forced Labour' Tariff Findings; Calls Them Legally Flawed
summary: India has decided to formally contest a US trade action that imposed tariffs based on 'forced labour' findings related to Indian goods. India's government called the findings 'legally flawed' and said it would challenge them through appropriate trade dispute mechanisms. This development comes amid broader India-US tariff negotiations following the pause on reciprocal tariffs announced earlier in 2026.
exam_angle: India-US trade relations, WTO dispute settlement mechanisms, and tariff policy connect to GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy); 'forced labour' provisions under US trade law (UFLPA) are relevant.
key_facts: Issue: US tariffs based on 'forced labour' findings on Indian goods
India's response: Called findings legally flawed; to contest formally
Mechanism: WTO Dispute Settlement Body or bilateral trade talks
Context: Broader India-US tariff negotiations ongoing in 2026

title: AI Hiring Outpaces Overall IT Recruitment in India
summary: A new report reveals that hiring for Artificial Intelligence-related roles in India is outpacing overall IT sector recruitment, signalling a structural shift in India's technology employment landscape. Companies across sectors — from IT services to BFSI and manufacturing — are aggressively hiring AI/ML engineers, data scientists, and prompt engineers. This trend reflects India's aspiration to become a global AI hub, supported by the IndiaAI Mission.
exam_angle: AI workforce trends connect to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) and GS Paper 2 (Governance — digital economy); India's AI policy (IndiaAI Mission, National AI Strategy) is exam-relevant.
key_facts: Trend: AI hiring growing faster than overall IT recruitment in India
Key roles: AI/ML engineers, data scientists, prompt engineers
Policy context: IndiaAI Mission launched 2024; ₹10,300 crore budget
India aims to be a global AI hub under Digital India framework
